title: Flatness of a finitely presented algebra map descends to a stage of a directed colimit of base rings
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings (ring maps $A_i\to A_{i'}$ for $i\le i'$, the identity for $i=i'$, compatible with composition), with colimit $A=\varinjlim_iA_i$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $0\in I$, let $B_0$ and $C_0$ be commutative $A_0$-algebras and $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ a homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras which is of finite presentation, i.e. $C_0$ is a finitely presented $B_0$-algebra via $\varphi_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For $i\ge0$ regard $A_i$ as an $A_0$-algebra via the transition map and $A$ via the coprojection $A_0\to A$, and put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi_i=\mathrm{id}_{A_i}\otimes\varphi_0:B_i\to C_i$, and $B=A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C=A\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\varphi_0:B\to C$. If $\varphi$ is a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then there is $i_0\in I$ with $i_0\ge0$ such that $\varphi_i:B_i\to C_i$ is a flat ring map for every $i\ge i_0$.
